forcedChoices.choice: Spanish word followed by the English word in parentheses for each of the nine words
forcedChoices.reason: The sentence depends on the magical origin of the English words; some Spanish forms (hechizado, encantador, atónito) keep that origin, the others do not, so the English word stays visible.
The glossary term 'reversión' has the coined sense of the Reversion Directors (30:3.7); here the word means a fall back to older beliefs.
'fantasmas' is the form for 'ghosts' in this paper; a separate word keeps the two apart.

forcedChoices.choice: símbolos del grupo y su dios
forcedChoices.reason: The English can mean symbols of the group and of their god, or symbols of the group and also their god; the Spanish keeps both readings open.
'magos' is used for 'magicians' in 88:6.1 and 'brujos' is the glossary form for 'witch doctors'; a separate word keeps the three apart.
